kid.question: What kind of words can the Lord help His servant speak to someone who is tired?

options.text: A sharp rebuke to the proud
A warning to those who refuse to listen
A song of victory over enemies
A timely word to the weary

kid.explanation: Isaiah 50:4 states this teaching: A timely word to the weary.

kid.question: How did the servant respond when the Lord opened his ear?

options.text: He hid from the people who mocked him
He chose to rely on his own light
He listened and did not turn back
He refused to hear the Lord

kid.explanation: Isaiah 50:5 states this teaching: He listened and did not turn back.

kid.question: What did the servant allow his enemies to do?

options.text: Mock him without touching him
Strike his back and shame him
Take away his cloak
Bind him and leave him in a pit

kid.explanation: Isaiah 50:6 states this teaching: Strike his back and shame him.

kid.question: Why was the servant not overcome by shame?

options.text: The Lord God would help him
He knew the people would praise him
He had never faced an enemy before
He could hide from every accusation

kid.explanation: Isaiah 50:7 states this teaching: The Lord God would help him.

kid.question: Who is near to justify the servant?

options.text: The servant’s accuser
Jerusalem’s watchman
Abraham
The Lord

kid.explanation: Isaiah 50:8 states this teaching: The Lord.

kid.question: What should a person do when walking in darkness without light?

options.text: Fear the reproach of people
Wait until the oppressor grows weak
Trust in the Lord and rely on God
Light a fire and trust its sparks

kid.explanation: Isaiah 50:10 states this teaching: Trust in the Lord and rely on God.

kid.question: What does Isaiah tell seekers of righteousness to remember?

options.text: To remind covenant seekers of their roots and God’s power to increase them
The rock and pit from which they were taken
Abraham and Sarah
Like Eden, a garden of joy

kid.explanation: Isaiah 51:1 supports this answer: He calls them to look back to their beginnings..

kid.question: Which faithful couple should Israel remember?

options.text: Abraham and Sarah
The rock and pit from which they were taken
Like Eden, a garden of joy
To remind covenant seekers of their roots and God’s power to increase them

kid.explanation: Isaiah 51:2 supports this answer: Isaiah points to Abraham and Sarah as their ancestors..

kid.question: What will the Lord make Zion’s wilderness become?

options.text: The rock and pit from which they were taken
Abraham and Sarah
To remind covenant seekers of their roots and God’s power to increase them
Like Eden, a garden of joy

kid.explanation: Isaiah 51:3 supports this answer: The Lord promises comfort and makes the waste places like Eden..

kid.question: What should people with God’s law in their hearts not fear?

options.text: The cup of trembling
Their own need to seek righteousness
People’s reproach and insults
The Lord’s correction

kid.explanation: Isaiah 51:7 states this teaching: People’s reproach and insults.

high-school.question: What links the servant’s ability to help the weary with his own discipleship?

options.text: He listened and did not turn back
Strike his back and shame him
He first listens to the Lord and does not rebel
A timely word to the weary

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 50:4-5 supports this answer: The passage connects an opened ear and obedience with speaking helpfully..

high-school.question: What contrast explains the servant’s confidence despite public humiliation?

options.text: Strike his back and shame him
He is shamed by people but helped by God
A timely word to the weary
He listened and did not turn back

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 50:6-7 supports this answer: Verse 7 grounds his resolve in the Lord’s help..

high-school.question: What contrast does Isaiah make between trusting God and relying on self-made light?

options.text: Trusting God leads one to rely on Him; self-kindled sparks end in sorrow
Trust in the Lord and rely on God
People’s reproach and insults
Creation wears away, but the Lord’s salvation and righteousness endure

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 50:10-11 supports this answer: The two verses distinguish reliance on God from self-directed light..

high-school.question: Why does Isaiah pair the image of a rock with Abraham and Sarah?

options.text: The rock and pit from which they were taken
Abraham and Sarah
Like Eden, a garden of joy
To remind covenant seekers of their roots and God’s power to increase them

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 51:1-2 supports this answer: He links Israel’s origin to God calling and blessing Abraham..

high-school.question: What change does the promise about Zion’s waste places describe?

options.text: Abraham and Sarah
Like Eden, a garden of joy
The Lord can turn desolation into a place of joy and thanksgiving
The rock and pit from which they were taken

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 51:3 supports this answer: The verse names comfort, a garden, joy, and melody..

high-school.question: How does the Lord say His law will serve the nations?

options.text: He listened and did not turn back
It will become a light, while His saving power reaches the isles
His law becomes light while distant peoples wait for His arm
A timely word to the weary

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 51:4-5 supports this answer: Isaiah calls His judgment a light and describes distant peoples waiting on Him..

high-school.question: What enduring contrast should strengthen people facing mortality?

options.text: Creation wears away, but the Lord’s salvation and righteousness endure
Trust in the Lord and rely on God
People’s reproach and insults
Trusting God leads one to rely on Him; self-kindled sparks end in sorrow

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 51:6 supports this answer: Verse 6 contrasts the fading heavens and earth with lasting salvation..

high-school.question: What does having the Lord’s law in one’s heart change about public criticism?

options.text: Trust in the Lord and rely on God
People’s reproach and insults
Trusting God leads one to rely on Him; self-kindled sparks end in sorrow
It need not make the person afraid

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 51:7 supports this answer: The verse directly tells the righteous not to fear reproach..

high-school.question: Why does the servant invite an adversary to come near?

options.text: He listened and did not turn back
Strike his back and shame him
He trusts the Lord to help and justify him
A timely word to the weary

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 50:8-9 supports this answer: The servant’s challenge follows his confidence that God is near..

high-school.question: What is the movement from Abraham’s story to Zion’s future?

options.text: Like Eden, a garden of joy
God’s blessing of one family opens into comfort and renewal for Zion
The rock and pit from which they were taken
Abraham and Sarah

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 51:2-3 supports this answer: The verses move from Abraham’s increase to Zion made fruitful..

expert.question: How does the sequence in Isaiah 50:4–5 define the servant’s speech?

options.text: Strike his back and shame him
Receptive listening precedes obedient speech for the weary
A timely word to the weary
He listened and did not turn back

expert.explanation: Isaiah 50:4-5 supports this answer: The servant’s ear is opened before he speaks a timely word..

expert.question: What holds together the servant’s exposure to abuse and his challenge to accusers?

options.text: He accepts shame yet appeals to the Lord as his defender
A timely word to the weary
He listened and did not turn back
Strike his back and shame him

expert.explanation: Isaiah 50:6-9 supports this answer: The passage shifts from inflicted humiliation to divine help and justification..

People’s reproach and insults
Trusting God leads one to rely on Him; self-kindled sparks end in sorrow
Self-produced light cannot provide the faithful security offered by God

expert.explanation: Isaiah 50:10-11 supports this answer: Isaiah contrasts reliance on God with the sorrowful end of self-lit sparks..

expert.question: What does the “rock” and “pit” image contribute beyond naming ancestors?

options.text: Abraham and Sarah
Like Eden, a garden of joy
It makes Israel’s origin a reason to seek righteousness with hope
The rock and pit from which they were taken

expert.explanation: Isaiah 51:1-2 supports this answer: The next verse recalls God calling and multiplying Abraham..

expert.question: How do Eden, thanksgiving, and melody function together in the promise to Zion?

options.text: Like Eden, a garden of joy
They portray restoration as both renewed life and communal joy
The rock and pit from which they were taken
Abraham and Sarah

expert.explanation: Isaiah 51:3 supports this answer: Isaiah joins the garden image with gladness and singing..

expert.question: What parallel does the Lord draw between His law and His saving reach?

options.text: His law becomes light while distant peoples wait for His arm
It will become a light, while His saving power reaches the isles
A timely word to the weary
He listened and did not turn back

expert.explanation: Isaiah 51:4-5 supports this answer: Both verses extend the Lord’s work beyond Israel to the isles and peoples..

expert.question: Why does the comparison to smoke and an old garment sharpen the assurance of salvation?

options.text: Trust in the Lord and rely on God
People’s reproach and insults
Trusting God leads one to rely on Him; self-kindled sparks end in sorrow
It sets creation’s temporary state against God’s lasting righteousness

expert.explanation: Isaiah 51:6 supports this answer: The verse explicitly contrasts perishing creation with salvation forever..

expert.question: How does Isaiah define the audience able to withstand reproach?

options.text: People’s reproach and insults
Trusting God leads one to rely on Him; self-kindled sparks end in sorrow
They know righteousness and carry the Lord’s law in their hearts
Trust in the Lord and rely on God

expert.explanation: Isaiah 51:7 supports this answer: Verse 7 identifies both traits before commanding them not to fear..

expert.question: What reasoning supports the servant’s refusal to be confounded?

options.text: Strike his back and shame him
God helps, justifies, and outlasts every accuser
A timely word to the weary
He listened and did not turn back

expert.explanation: Isaiah 50:7-9 supports this answer: The servant names divine help and the decay of his opponents..

The rock and pit from which they were taken

Like Eden, a garden of joy
